name: SplitPolyIntoTwoPolys
formula: =LAMBDA(vertices,xp,yp,xq,yq,LET(n, ROWS(vertices), pointsWithIntersections, {ref}InsertPolyAndLineIntersection(vertices, xp, yp, xq, yq), isIntersection, CHOOSECOLS(pointsWithIntersections, 3), start_index, XMATCH(TRUE, isIntersection, 0, 1), end_index, XMATCH(TRUE, isIntersection, 0, -1), shape1, UNIQUE(DROP(CHOOSEROWS(pointsWithIntersections, SEQUENCE(end_index - start_index + 1, , start_index)), , -2)), shape2, UNIQUE(DROP(VSTACK(TAKE(pointsWithIntersections, start_index), DROP(pointsWithIntersections, end_index - 1)), , -2)), isShape1, IF(ROWS(shape1) > 2, TRUE, FALSE), isShape2, IF(ROWS(shape2) > 2, TRUE, FALSE), shape1_text, ARRAYTOTEXT(shape1, 1), shape2_text, ARRAYTOTEXT(shape2, 1), result, IFS(AND(isShape1, isShape2), VSTACK(shape1_text, shape2_text), isShape1, shape1_text, isShape2, shape2_text), result))
comment: Splits one polygon at the intersections of a segment. vertices is an n×2 array of (x, y) rows in order; the last vertex connects to the first. The segment is (xp, yp) to (xq, yq). The result is one or two rows. Each row is a strict ARRAYTOTEXT of one piece as (x, y) rows, from the first intersection to the last and the wrap-around piece. A segment that misses returns #N/A. Fewer than two columns returns #REF!. Last Update at 2026-11-03.
